verdict.rationale: Helix Cloud documents role-based access control and scoped API keys (read-only, read-write, or operation-restricted) on Bearer-authenticated requests, with permission scopes such as database.query.read on MCP tools. Per-collection or per-resource permissions are not documented, and tenancy isolation is described as row-level and left to the application layer. Missing for 10: per-collection permissions, depth of role definitions, evidence that these controls apply to self-hosted/local instances, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can enforce granular access control (API keys, roles, per-collection permissions) on database operations

citations.quote: Role-based access control. Scoped API keys with read-only, read-write, or operation-restricted permissions for least-privilege credentials per service or environment.
All API requests to Helix Cloud are authenticated with a Bearer token. Tokens are managed through the Helix dashboard.
helix_execute_read_query: execute exact v3 request_type: "read" JSON; requires database.query.read.
